block_caveats.swiftui.alert: Windows TaskDialog compared by semantics; main-window pixels reported, never a gate (docs/sr1-status.md block 17).
block_caveats.swiftui.animation: One explicit transaction per flush decides for every changed node; spring cases use a 2 px extent tolerance (docs/sr1-status.md block 18; decisions C1-C6). No Animatable, keyframes or TimelineView in the block's symbol list.
block_caveats.swiftui.binding: Setter transaction, constant, derived bindings (docs/sr1-status.md block 12).
block_caveats.swiftui.button: Every style measured in light only; pressed and focused states unmeasured; bordered and prominent are 7-8 px narrower (docs/sr1-status.md block 11).
block_caveats.swiftui.color-scheme: Semantic colours measured light and dark; toggle artwork at scale 2.5 only (docs/sr1-status.md block 20).
block_caveats.swiftui.custom-layout: Layout protocol, left-to-right and right-to-left, exact (docs/sr1-status.md block 5).
block_caveats.swiftui.focus-state: UIA keyboard focus is false in the Sandbox; gated through @FocusState text (docs/sr1-status.md block 14).
block_caveats.swiftui.image: SF Symbols map to Segoe Fluent Icons; 41 symbol sizes use measured ink overrides; glyph shape is reported, not gated (docs/sr1-decisions.md decision 3; docs/sr1-status.md 'Known gaps').
block_caveats.swiftui.ime-marked-text: Posted WM_IME messages only; real composition needs hardware (docs/sr1-status.md block 15).
block_caveats.swiftui.list: No scrolling, no sidebar or grouped styles, no dark appearance, no multi-selection adjacency (docs/sr1-decisions.md A10).
block_caveats.swiftui.opacity-transition: Image fade excluded; no .scale or custom Transition (docs/sr1-status.md block 19).
block_caveats.swiftui.padding-frame: padding all, per edge, EdgeInsets; fixed and flexible frames, 9 alignments (docs/sr1-status.md block 9).
block_caveats.swiftui.preference-key: Custom reduce, nil default, first contribution wins (docs/sr1-status.md block 10).
block_caveats.swiftui.scroll-view: No ScrollViewReader or scrollPosition in the runtime; vertical offset 0, bottom anchor and horizontal axis measured (docs/sr1-status.md blocks 6).
block_caveats.swiftui.shapes.fill-stroke: Continuous stroke only; hairline strokes below 1.5 px untested (docs/sr1-status.md 'Known gaps'). Path, trim and dashes are not in this block's symbol list.
block_caveats.swiftui.stack-overlay: ZStack and overlay only (factory/registry/manifest.json); VStack and HStack have no manifest entry.
block_caveats.swiftui.text.bundled-font: Segoe UI is the Windows body font, so glyph pixels are excluded (decision 2); the bundled Tinos font is exact through ABI 0.7.
block_caveats.swiftui.textfield: Windows focus ring not drawn; real IME and TSF deferred to hardware (docs/sr1-status.md block 13).
block_caveats.swiftui.toggle: Switch and checkbox styles, measured at scale 2.5, light and dark (decisions 7, 8, D2).

journeys.name: Resting pill and open notch
journeys.summary: The always-present notch: a pill at the chosen edge that is open with every ring visible, drawn as one liquid silhouette on all four edges.
journeys.windows_note: Windows draws the same cells in a software rasteriser into a layered window per monitor (windows/README.md 'The notch'); comparison rows 'Resting/Expanded notch' all match. Windows has no surface style or colour transition (docs/settings.md 'Still to add on Windows').

journeys.name: Hover open, peek and fold
journeys.summary: Pointer contact opens the pill; events peek it open for 3, 5 or 10 seconds; a full-screen app folds it away.
journeys.windows_note: Show: Always show, On hover or Hidden, folds for a borderless full-monitor window (windows/README.md 'The notch'); peek length is a Windows setting too (docs/settings.md, 'Peek length').

journeys.name: Ring gauges (Claude, Codex, System, Disks)
journeys.summary: Per-provider cells: a glyph in a usage ring, an inner thin ring, colour bands, weekly headline and pace.
journeys.windows_note: Windows has the five cells (windows/README.md 'The notch'). Differs: no inner activity arc while an agent works (docs/comparison/behaviour.md row 10, high), no refresh press-in (row 11), CPU and Memory are one System ring (docs/settings.md 'Still to add on Windows'), no daily pace ring.

journeys.name: Hover cards and session list
journeys.summary: A card slides out of the notch on a neck for each ring: limit windows, resets, plan, account, drives, GPU, session rows.
journeys.windows_note: Windows has the hover cards (windows/src/card.rs; comparison group 'Notch: hover-card' is low-severity glyph differences only). Windows lacks the running-session list and session-row click (behaviour.md rows 12-13, high and med).

journeys.name: Send and LocalSend nearby share
journeys.summary: The fifth cell: device picker card, drop target, Cmd-V to send the clipboard, transfer progress, incoming-share toast.
journeys.windows_note: Windows has the Send cell with device rows, drop or Ctrl+V, progress and Accept/Decline (windows/README.md 'Nearby sharing'; behaviour.md 'Checked, no material difference: Send'). Gap: Chat rows on the Send card (behaviour.md row 14, med). The LocalSend protocol runs in the hub on both platforms (windows/src/send.rs:3).

journeys.name: Tools cell and middle-click wheel
journeys.summary: The sixth cell lists one-tap tools; the middle button opens a liquid ring of tools round the pointer.
journeys.windows_note: Windows has the wheel and Tools card (windows/README.md 'Tools'). The tool set differs from the Mac's (behaviour.md row 28, written 12 October when Windows had no notes, clipboard or task-view; docs/settings.md lists the current Windows wheel default, which now includes Clipboard). Comparison group 'Notch: wheel' is five low-severity glyph rows.

journeys.name: Launcher
journeys.summary: Option+Space panel: apps, files, calculator, clipboard rows, snippets, notes, custom commands.
journeys.windows_note: Windows launcher exists, off by default (windows/README.md 'Launcher'); Mac-only sources: dictionary, Apple Shortcuts, per-app hotkeys, content search, snippet expansion (docs/settings.md 'Still to add on Windows'; behaviour.md rows 38-40).

journeys.name: Clipboard history strip
journeys.summary: A strip of clip cards with boards, filters, preview and paste-back.
journeys.windows_note: Windows strip landed on 2026-10-13 (docs/settings.md 'Clipboard' rows; windows/src/clip_strip.rs); a few spec parts are still open (docs/settings.md 'Still to add on Windows').

journeys.name: Settings entry points and hub hand-off
journeys.summary: Settings bulb with its neck, the move grip, click-to-open-hub on each ring, right-click Quit; the hub is a separate process.
journeys.windows_note: Windows has the Settings disc, move grip, right-click Quit and hub launch (windows/README.md 'The notch', hub.rs:1-9, bridge.rs:1-9). Differs: permission-dot click and outside-ring click (behaviour.md rows 24-25), relaunch route to Settings when hidden (row 27).

journeys.name: Alerts, toasts and notifications
journeys.summary: Usage reset, limit reached, drive filling, session ended: a toast from the notch, a system banner, a chime.
journeys.windows_note: Windows has the toast queue, hover hold and reset, limit, drive, agent and update toasts (windows/README.md 'Toasts'; windows/src/alerts.rs). Toasts now come out in every Show state, including a Hidden notch (windows/README.md 'Toasts'), which closes the high-severity row 15 of docs/comparison/behaviour.md (written 12 October). Delivery and sound rows 17-23 are still listed as differences.

journeys.name: Multi-display, placement and edges
journeys.summary: One notch per display, four edges, Option-drag along and round corners, per-display scope and preference.
journeys.windows_note: Windows has one panel per monitor with its own edge and position (behaviour.md row 26, Windows-only). Missing on Windows: display choice and which displays (`displayPreference`, `notchScope`; docs/settings.md 'Still to add on Windows'); comparison rows 'appearance/all-displays', 'main-display' are windows-missing.

journeys.name: Accounts (Claude and Codex)
journeys.summary: Which account each ring reads, account switch, the Sync chats button on the Claude card, credentials read, plan and sign-in rows.
journeys.windows_note: Windows reads one Claude account (no per-folder profiles), no Sign in action, no reset-credit extras (behaviour.md rows 1-5, high and med). Account rename and forget match (behaviour.md 'Checked, no material difference'). The hub's Accounts section is shared.

journeys.name: Updates and the disk-image installer
journeys.summary: Update card (Update/Later), restart-after-update, and the disk-image card that installs, replaces or undoes an app.
journeys.windows_note: Windows has update cards (windows/src/update.rs) and an installer card for new .msi/.msix/.exe downloads (windows/src/installer.rs); the trigger differs by platform (behaviour.md row 35, accepted) and auto-install defaults differ (rows 32-34, med).

journeys.name: Keyboard and window conveniences (no notch UI)
journeys.summary: Fn as Command, window moves, Finder cut and paste, Auto Quit, Dock click, snippet expansion.
journeys.windows_note: Windows has Alt-as-Ctrl editing keys and 34 window chords (windows/README.md 'Editing keys and window shortcuts'); Auto Quit, snippet expansion and Dock-click minimise are missing or redundant (behaviour.md rows 41-45).

journeys.name: Agent session activity
journeys.summary: Watches Claude, Codex and Pi sessions: activity arc on the ring, finished-session peek, terminal tab focus.
journeys.windows_note: Windows has no session monitor; its 'agent turn ended' toast is inferred from transcript writes and is off by default (behaviour.md rows 10, 12, 13, 18; windows/src/alerts.rs `finish_loop`).

journeys.name: Uninstall helper, Finder extension and elevation
journeys.summary: Privileged launch daemon that moves apps to the Trash, the Finder Sync menu, the elevation client.
journeys.windows_note: Mac-only by platform: Windows apps are removed through their own uninstaller (behaviour.md row 58, accepted) and Explorer has its own Copy as path (row 44).

journeys.name: View-shot harness (CI acceptance pictures)
journeys.summary: Renders every view in qa/notch-views.json on the Mac; the Windows side renders the same list for the comparison.
journeys.windows_note: windows/src/viewshots.rs renders the same list (windows/README.md 'Checks'); docs/comparison/README.md holds the pairs.

services.name: Accessibility API automation (AXUIElement, AXObserver, AXIsProcessTrusted)
services.rightkit: desktop-automation: rightkit-automation 0.1.0 (staged-unverified, AX and UIA); Swift RightKitAccessibility 'designed' (pulse/STATUS.md)
services.sr2: Mac extension module plus an automation adapter; not a view block
services.windows: UI Automation only for link detection under a middle click (windows/src/wheel.rs:1893-1927); window moves use SetWindowPos on the foreground window (windows/src/window_keys.rs:459-466). Auto Quit has no Windows version (docs/comparison/behaviour.md row 43).

services.name: CPU, memory and disk metrics (host_statistics, sysctl, vm_statistics, statfs, volume resource keys)
services.rightkit: none: `rightkit owns --compact` lists no system-metrics owner; pulse/STATUS-WINDOWS.md 'Ruled local' keeps sensors in Pulse
services.sr2: SensorService (new; not in architecture section 7)
services.windows: GetSystemTimes deltas, GlobalMemoryStatusEx, PDH counters and GetDiskFreeSpaceExW (windows/src/sensors.rs:2, :32, :36, :237); 2 s visible and 10 s hidden cadence (windows/src/lifecycle.rs:5-6).

services.name: IOKit sensors (IOAccelerator GPU utilisation, IOHIDEventSystemClient temperature)
services.rightkit: none (same as system-metrics)
services.sr2: SensorService: GPU busy and temperatures (Mac extension for IOKit)
services.windows: GPU temperature from an NVML helper started only while the System card is open, CPU zones from MSAcpi_ThermalZoneTemperature through a hidden PowerShell (windows/src/sensors.rs:11, :948-959, :992).

services.name: User notifications and sounds (UNUserNotificationCenter, NSSound)
services.rightkit: desktop-shell: rightkit-shell 0.1.4 (registry-recorded) / 0.2.0 (staged-unverified) lists notifications; Tauri-specific parts must be separated (docs/architecture.md section 7)
services.sr2: NotificationService: post, sound, permission state
services.windows: WinRT ToastNotificationManager through a hidden PowerShell under PowerShell's own AUMID (windows/src/notify.rs:5, :19, :94), stock sounds by PlaySoundW (windows/src/notify.rs:3, :64).

services.name: Launch at login and privileged daemon (SMAppService)
services.rightkit: desktop-shell: rightkit-shell lists autostart
services.sr2: LaunchService: launch at login
services.windows: One HKCU Run value, per user, no elevation (windows/src/autostart.rs:1-9). The Mac's privileged SMAppService.daemon has no Windows counterpart (docs/comparison/behaviour.md rows 50-51).

services.name: Open links, files and apps; running-application control (NSWorkspace, NSRunningApplication)
services.rightkit: owned-processes: rightkit-process 0.3.3 (registry-recorded); pulse/STATUS-WINDOWS.md asks for 0.4.0
services.sr2: LaunchService: open file, link, app
services.windows: Hub start and show-section through a child process and a named event (windows/src/hub.rs:1-9, :178); explorer.exe for 'show in folder' (windows/src/send.rs:2198).

services.name: Single-instance and app-to-hub signalling (Darwin notifications, Distributed notifications, CFNotificationCenter)
services.rightkit: desktop-shell: rightkit-shell (single instance); local-services: rightkit-service 0.1.4 (staged-unverified) for the hub channel
services.sr2: LaunchService (single instance) and EngineService (hub channel)
services.windows: Named mutex with newest-wins (windows/src/main.rs:735) and named events `Local\dev.orthic.pulse.hub.show.<section>` and `Local\dev.orthic.pulse.notch.state` (windows/src/hub.rs:1-9, windows/src/bridge.rs:1-9).

services.name: Keychain credential reads (SecItem, Keychain)
services.rightkit: os-credential-store: rightkit-secrets 0.1.3 (staged-unverified, Credential Manager) and RightKitSwift (rightkit-swift 0.4.0, registry-pinned; pulse/STATUS.md says tag 0.7.0 is in use, a version disagreement to settle)
services.sr2: SecureStore: read-only keychain item; file read on Windows
services.windows: No credential store: the Windows notch reads Claude Code's and Codex's own credential files read-only (windows/src/usage.rs:1-8; docs/comparison/behaviour.md header, usage.rs:989-995). The Mac reads the Keychain through RightKitAppleCredentials (mac/Notch/Sources/Providers/KeychainItem.swift:2).

services.name: Settings persistence (UserDefaults, @AppStorage, JSON state files)
services.rightkit: settings-persistence: rightkit-settings 0.1.1 (staged-unverified); waits on rightkit-fs 0.3.4 (pulse/STATUS-WINDOWS.md)
services.sr2: Settings adapter (rightkit-settings through the swiftright-services C ABI, docs/architecture.md section 7)
services.windows: pill-settings.json with an own bounded parser and a restricted-ACL atomic writer (windows/src/settings.rs:1-10; pulse/STATUS-WINDOWS.md 'Blocked on RightKit').

services.name: Clipboard (NSPasteboard, change count, paste)
services.rightkit: desktop-shell: @rightkit/shell lists rich clipboard (0.1.0, declaration-only); the clipboard store is a held row until RightKit answers (pulse/STATUS-WINDOWS.md)
services.sr2: ClipboardService: read/write types, change observation, sensitive-content policy
services.windows: AddClipboardFormatListener worker (windows/src/clip_capture.rs:2, windows/src/clip_win.rs:42) and OpenClipboard reads (windows/src/send_sys.rs:51, :224).

services.name: Drag and drop (NSDraggingSource, onDrop, onDrag, NSItemProvider)
services.rightkit: none found in `rightkit owns --compact`
services.sr2: ClipboardService / DialogService: drop target
services.windows: WM_DROPFILES and DragQueryFileW (windows/src/send_sys.rs:1-5, windows/src/clip_win.rs:49, :224).

services.name: File and directory watching (FSEvents, DispatchSource file system objects)
services.rightkit: file-watching: rightkit-watch 0.3.2 (staged-unverified); Windows backend 'not started' (pulse/STATUS.md, STATUS-WINDOWS.md); the Mac notch already imports RightKitWatch (2 files)
services.sr2: Watch adapter (new; not in architecture section 7)
services.windows: Three ReadDirectoryChangesW watchers on their own threads (windows/src/claude_watch.rs:1-5).

services.name: Child processes and shell commands (Foundation.Process, posix_spawn)
services.rightkit: owned-processes: rightkit-process 0.3.3 (registry-recorded); 0.4.0 requested
services.sr2: EngineService: child process lifecycle
services.windows: std::process::Command for the hub, drive health and installers (windows/src/hub.rs:178, windows/src/drive_health.rs:182, windows/src/installer.rs:1117).

services.name: Privileged helper over XPC and Apple Events (NSXPCConnection, NSAppleScript, Apple Events)
services.rightkit: none
services.sr2: Mac extension module only
services.windows: No equivalent: Windows apps are removed through their own uninstaller (docs/comparison/behaviour.md row 58, accepted difference).

services.name: Local-network discovery and sharing (Network.framework, Bonjour, NWListener, URLSession)
services.rightkit: http-client: rightkit-http 0.2.5 (staged-unverified); Send engine: rightkit-send 'unpublished' (pulse/STATUS.md); local-services: rightkit-service 0.1.4
services.sr2: EngineService (nearby-share engine in the hub) plus an HTTP adapter
services.windows: LocalSend runs in the hub's core on both platforms (windows/src/send.rs:3); the notch makes WinHTTP calls for usage and updates (windows/src/http.rs:25).

services.name: Core Animation layers and display links (CALayer, CAShapeLayer, CADisplayLink, CVDisplayLink)
services.rightkit: none (renderer)
services.sr2: Not a service: SwiftRight renderer, animation and clock (SR1 blocks 18-19)
services.windows: A software rasteriser stepped by a 16 ms timer only while something moves (windows/src/motion.rs:1-6, windows/src/canvas.rs:3).

services.name: System materials and glass (NSVisualEffectView, glassEffect)
services.rightkit: none (renderer)
services.sr2: Not a service: renderer foundation (SR1 plan, Foundations)
services.windows: None: the Windows notch is solid; surface style and colour transition are listed as still to add (pulse/docs/settings.md, 'Still to add on Windows').

services.name: Finder Sync extension and Finder automation
services.rightkit: none
services.sr2: Mac extension module only
services.windows: None: Explorer has its own Copy as path and Open in Terminal (docs/comparison/behaviour.md row 44).

services.name: Disk images, code signing and Gatekeeper (hdiutil, SecStaticCode, spctl, ditto)
services.rightkit: update-policy: @rightkit/updates 0.2.5 (JS, Tauri); signing and publication are RightKit release tooling
services.sr2: Mac extension module; Windows needs its own installer-check adapter
services.windows: Installer card for new .msi, .msix and setup .exe downloads (windows/src/installer.rs:5-8); update download checked with WinVerifyTrust (windows/src/update.rs:10).

services.name: Screenshots (screencapture, CGWindowListCreateImage, ScreenCaptureKit, CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess)
services.rightkit: none (desktop-qa and screen-recording owners do not cover product capture)
services.sr2: CaptureService (new; not in architecture section 7)
services.windows: BitBlt from the screen DC after the overlay is gone, CF_DIB to the clipboard (windows/src/shot.rs:16).

services.name: Privacy-permission state probes (TCC, Full Disk Access, local network, Accessibility prompt)
services.rightkit: none
services.sr2: Mac extension module only
services.windows: None needed: Windows needs no permission grants; the hub shows startup, notifications and firewall (pulse/README.md 'Permissions'; docs/comparison/behaviour.md row 50).

services.name: Logging and diagnostics (os.Logger, os_log, NSLog)
services.rightkit: structured-logging: rightkit-logs 0.2.1 (staged-unverified; Mac notch imports RightKitDiagnostics, mac/Notch/Sources/App/Log.swift:3); crash-reporting: rightkit-crash 0.2.1
services.sr2: Diagnostics adapter (docs/architecture.md section 7, 'Diagnostics and native QA')
services.windows: diag.rs writes notch.log (windows/README.md 'Diagnostics'); crashes through rightkit-crash 0.2.1 (pulse/STATUS-WINDOWS.md).
